source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Leviticus 26–27. The exact original XML records include all three annotations at 26:7, 26:8 and 26:28; no numbering shift occurs in this batch.

key_decisions.decision: Keeps all four prohibited objects and selects on it for the stone’s preposition; a note preserves the uncertain installation and before-it alternative.
Keeps the dwelling image and strong abhorrence verb, anticipating its reversal in verse 30 rather than weakening it to dislike.
Preserves slavery, broken yoke bars and bodily upright walking rather than replacing the ancient image with an abstract freedom slogan.
Keeps rejection, abhorrence, refusal and covenant-breaking as connected actions rather than a vague failure to obey.
Preserves divine agency, both illness terms and bodily images without assigning a modern diagnosis; crop clarifies what enemies eat.
Keeps face-against as the reversal of turning toward, names hostile rule and retains the no-pursuer fear pattern.
Clarifies pride-of-strength while retaining both metal images instead of replacing them with drought alone.
Uses hostility provisionally for qeri and retains walking, refusal and sevenfold blows; a note identifies the rare word’s uncertainty.
Makes the bereavement verb’s human cost explicit and preserves livestock loss, population reduction and empty roads.
Preserves reciprocal hostility, emphatic divine subject and another sevenfold stage.
Keeps covenant vengeance, city gathering, pestilence and enemy capture without flattening these into one generic punishment.
Retains staff-of-bread with a compact explanation, ten women, one oven and weighed rations; hunger reverses verse 5.
Retains the added fury and emphatic agent as the hostility sequence reaches its fourth sevenfold warning.
Preserves the explicit cannibalism, both sexes and repeated eating clause, without euphemizing the horror or adding circumstances absent from this verse.
Keeps disputed cult installation provisionally as incense altars, preserves corpse/corpse wordplay and the reversal of verse 11.
Retains plural sanctuaries and the sensory rejection of the recurrent offering-aroma formula.
Keeps dispersal, drawn sword and separate land/city consequences as the earlier pursuit promise is reversed.
Retains both Sabbath-enjoyment clauses and the land as subject; note preserves making-up-for-rest as another sense of ratsah.
Keeps survivors, inward fear, the slight leaf sound and the repeated no-pursuer paradox without converting dread into a modern psychiatric diagnosis.
Preserves stumbling and absent pursuit; stand is selected for the rare tequmah, with possible absence of a defender noted.
Retains the land’s devouring image rather than replacing it with a generalized exile statement.
Keeps both wasting clauses and intergenerational guilt; the compressed with-them relationship is made intelligible without shifting blame solely to ancestors.
Selects a declarative continuation rather than inserting if; preserves confession of both generations and repeated hostility, with conditional alternative noted.
Keeps reciprocal hostility and the uncircumcised-heart image; then perhaps represents uncertain o az, with alternatives noted alongside ratsah’s penalty sense.
Keeps land rest and guilt-payment connected through the repeated Hebrew root, and renders the doubled causal phrase emphatically.
Retains the limit on rejection and destruction rather than contradicting verse 30 with an unqualified claim of no abhorrence.
